checks: For positive f-mass of a closed convex L, absolute continuity gives positive Lebesgue measure, so int L is nonempty and its null boundary may be discarded. U'=U∩int L is therefore a nonempty open convex set. The new measure is unchanged by discarding the boundary. The stated exhaustion sets are compact, nested and contained in U'; the interior-distance condition is convex because the open ball of radius 1/n around a convex combination is contained in U' whenever the corresponding endpoint balls are. Their union is U', with the whole-space case covered by balls.

The finite positive convex inverse power on U' is continuous, hence so is f there. On each compact convex exhaustion set f is bounded and its zero extension is upper semicontinuous, since any approach from outside gives zero and the set is closed. For positive-mass truncations the positive set has interior; extending the inverse power by +∞ outside that set gives a convex function. These are exactly the hypotheses of d6a3cbae1da72277.

Each truncation's depth witness gives at least γ_q times its mass for the full restricted measure at that witness, because every halfspace dominates the truncated mass. This bounds the supremum of depth; it does not assume convergence of witnesses. The monotone mass limit gives the desired lower bound. Through-point halfspace masses are jointly continuous by dominated convergence and hyperplane nullity; minimization over the compact unit sphere yields continuous depth. The outward halfspace gives decay at infinity, and any point outside U' admits a containing separating or supporting halfspace with zero mass. Thus the positive maximum is attained inside U'⊂L. The argument holds for each positive-mass closed convex remainder of the same support, including unbounded remainders.

The choice of any inclusion-minimal I is fixed before α and all remainders. For j=1 the selected cap has mass V, giving (V−α)_++α≥V with γ₀=1. For j≥2 proper original normals imply ρ≥1. When ρ<j, projection to their span gives proper projected halfspaces with the same cap masses, and they cover the entire projected body by the original cover. Orthogonal Fubini gives the section-volume density; Brunn–Minkowski and the section inclusion make its (D−ρ)th root concave on the positive set if D>ρ, and thus it is log-concave. When ρ=D the uniform density is used directly. The interior of the projected body equals the projection of int K: extend a segment from the projection of an interior representative beyond the desired interior point, lift its endpoint, and take the strict convex combination. This ensures the correct open positive representative and closed convex support. Rank one is included: j=2 is the only minimal rank-one case with j≥2 since equal-orientation half-lines are nested, and the constant is γ₁=1/2.

When ρ=j≥2, independent original normals give a surjective affine margin map. Separating its image of K from the open negative orthant gives a nonzero λ with λ·ℓ≥sup over the orthant. Any negative λ_i would make the supremum +∞, so λ≥0 and the supremum is zero. If λ_i were zero, the positively weighted subfamily would already cover K pointwise, including where t=0, contradicting minimality. Therefore all λ_i>0 and the affine function t=λ·ℓ is nonconstant by independence. Linear coordinates on the margin space followed by affine completion on the original space preserve homogeneity of the selected margins in (v,t) and satisfy the frozen projective lemma's hypotheses with r=j−1.

The projected margins at (z,1) have positively weighted sum 1 everywhere and their closed positive halfspaces cover the full image space. If any projected normal vanished, that selected original margin would be proportional to t, impossible because t combines every independent original normal with positive coefficient and j≥2. The chart is fixed and the discarded set t=0 is volume-null, so total and cap masses match. The inverse power is −1/j. These are the inputs to hereditary depth and then trimming for the same projected family on every convex remainder.

The constants are ordered in the correct direction: for q>0, the derivative of q log(1+1/q) is log(1+1/q)−1/(q+1)>0; γ₀=1 is above γ₁=1/2. With min(ρ,j−1)≤s, replacing α/γ_min by α/γ_s raises the left side, strictly when the indices differ and α>0. Restoring omitted nonnegative terms gives the all-cover profile. Substituting α=min_i A_i gives exactly the stated overlap bound, including the zero-minimum union-bound case. The statement is weak inequality, not a general strictness or equality classification; α=0 can also give equality for a disjoint-a.e. cover.

For 2≤m≤D+1, canonical caps of an s-simplex times an unrestricted positive-volume factor cover by the sum of its barycentric coordinates. The homothety ratio s/(s+1) yields exactly A_i=γ_s V. Taking α=γ_s V gives equality, and replacing γ_s by any larger g makes α/g<V while every positive-part term stays zero. For m>D+1, appended proper halfspaces disjoint from K preserve this sharpness test, even with zero minimum; they do not witness positive-minimum overlap equality. Repeating canonical caps (the indexed statement allows repetition) preserves common positive mass and yields that equality too, because all A_i=α and α/γ_D=V. For m=1, α=V gives the analogous strict obstruction for g>1. For m=3,D≥2 the exact specialization is γ₂=4/9 and overlap coefficient 3−9/4=3/4.
